text:
PKIX-jy95 decision frontier is empty (children .1-.6 all closed; .9 OSCAL closed wontfix per same-day reversal). Bridge child epics filed: .7 pkix-zlint-bridge (open), .8 pkix-pkilint-bridge (open). The adapter-crate implementation epics for pkix-policy-zlint and pkix-policy-pkilint themselves (thin Lint-trait wrappers over the bridges, per .6 decision) are NOT filed. Two paths forward, both defensible:

(A) File those adapter-implementation epics now as PKIX-jy95.10 (pkix-policy-zlint, blocked on .7) and PKIX-jy95.11 (pkix-policy-pkilint, blocked on .8), then close PKIX-jy95 with reason "decision frontier empty; full adapter-crate child structure filed." Makes the parent epic's stated deliverable ("one child epic per crate") literally complete. Pro: clean tracking surface, parent epic stops appearing on bd ready. Con: design for those adapter crates is settled but trivially so (.6 memory: "thin Lint-trait wrappers") — the implementation epics carry almost no design content and may be premature.

(B) Defer filing the adapter-implementation epics until the bridge crates (.7 / .8) actually land — at that point file .10 / .11 as concrete "wrap this bridge in a Lint impl" work. Pro: matches the prelaunch "design for the eventual complete shape" rule without over-eagerly populating bd with implementations whose design is genuinely trivial; the adapter crates' shape may shift when the bridge is concrete. Con: PKIX-jy95 stays open and re-surfaces on bd ready each session as a P2 "ready" bead with no actionable autonomous work.

Recommendation: (A). The cost of filing two tracker epics is low; the architecture is settled; closing PKIX-jy95 cleanly stops re-triggering this question each session. The PKIX prelaunch framing (AGENTS.md "design for the eventual complete shape") argues for completing the planning surface.

Labeled human and moving on per do-beads protocol; not autonomously filing .10 / .11 or closing the parent — that's a planning-surface call for the human to make.
